target_customer: Mobile photographers and iPhone users who wanted professional looking edits, plus pro photographers who could sell their editing styles
problem: Phone photo filters looked generic. Priime offered editing styles built from the real editing workflows of professional photographers, and later RAW editing and photo sharing for photographers.
business_model: Consumer app with paid style packs sold a la carte, with a marketplace idea for photographer made filters

founders.name: Arthur Chang
founders.background_notes: YC page lists software engineering (web, mobile), filmmaking and photography. Later founded Ravel.

founders.name: Loren Baxter
founders.background_notes: Later Head of Design at Remix (YC W15) per YC page.

founders.name: Joe Pestro
founders.background_notes: YC page lists technical product management and full-stack development.

founders.name: Andrew Ng
founders.background_notes: YC page bio lists only a curator role at lightmist.coffee. Not the AI researcher of the same name.

exit.reason: The company posted that it was discontinuing Priime Collections and Priime Galleries and keeping the iPhone and iPad RAW apps, because lossless photo sharing cost too much to offer at a workable price. The post date was not visible.

competitors.name: VSCO Cam
competitors.what: Camera and editing app with film emulation presets, which reviewers compared Priime against directly

technical_complexity.rationale: A filter and editing app for iOS is standard mobile engineering. A reviewer reported slow opening and weak basic editing tools on large images, so the engineering was not trivial but not research grade.

defensibility.rationale: Filters are easy to copy. The only differentiator was licensed styles from named photographers, which a rival could also commission.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: VSCO was already the established name among enthusiasts. No source found showing an incumbent copying or buying Priime.

market_need_then: Mobile photo editing was a crowded and active category in 2015, with reviews of VSCO alternatives and enthusiasts paying for presets. A reviewer noted a $66 a la carte price, showing some willingness to pay but also a price barrier.

identity.visual_style: A reviewer said the interface closely resembled VSCO.

branding.brand_signature: Styles derived from the editing process of named professional photographers
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by PetaPixel, Laughing Squid, Trend Hunter and several reviewers around the March 2015 launch.

brand_strength.rationale: Some launch press and reviews, but no evidence of a lasting community, and the spelling with a double i invites misspelling.

outcome_analysis: Priime launched out of YC W15 in March 2015 into a market where VSCO already led among mobile photo enthusiasts. It added RAW editing and a sharing and collections product. The company later wrote that lossless full resolution sharing cost too much to offer at a price customers would pay, and it discontinued Collections and Galleries while keeping the editing apps. The directory marks it inactive, and no acquisition was found. The cause of final inactivity is not public beyond that post.
notes: Company website field is empty in the directory. The $120K seed rests on a single database (CB Insights, seen via search snippet because the page returned 403). Startupintros dates a seed to 2014-11, which conflicts, so the date is unverified. The Slimdown post and CB Insights page could not be opened (403), so their content is from search summaries. Founder education was not found in any opened source. No cause of inactivity beyond the Slimdown post was found. The competitor list rests on one dated review that names VSCO.
